MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Fires on the token right after a comma when that comma introduces a tacked-on continuation/appositive phrase (e.g. ", Looking…", ", Places…", ", (6) ff.", ", we promise"), i.e. it marks the start-of-phrase word following a comma rather than the punctuation itself — and is strongly suppressed on clause-final periods/commas that close a sentence.

This neuron is a weak, low-coherence detector that fires at boundary tokens closing an enumeration/name-list or preceding a collective count or summary — e.g. the final comma in a run of usernames, the verb after "The pair", a numeric tally after "they all get", a surname ending an obituary name-string, and garbled mojibake fragments.
